proof_summary: Let \(N=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}-1\); modular exponentiation in \((\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)[\sqrt3]\) shows that \(2+\sqrt3\) has full order \(N+1\), using the three prime divisors \(2,3,100943\) of \(N+1\) and coprime residue witnesses for the corresponding quotient powers. If \(N\) were composite, its least prime factor \(p\) would have \(p^2\le N\), whereas that order in \((\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)[\sqrt3]^\times\), whose size is less than \(p^2\), forces \(N+1<p^2\); thus \(N\) is prime and the exponent \(39101\) gives a positive witness.
